nodes.title: Correction of fd-dry-matrix-blind-to-the-reply-layer. 'A give-up with help spent gets no key' survived director20 because its dry predicate was too narrow (it knew only 'aap batao' and 'pata nahi, aap', and required a re-said sentence), not because the fault lives only in the reply layer. With the predicate widened (any bare 'pata nahi' / 'nahi pata' / 'aap batao' / 'nahi aata'; help spent once the card had a miss or was said twice; the turn must say the key) the dry walk fails on the same three rows as the live run plus c5-t02 offtopic 24: the walk itself drops the key before any model text exists. The repair seen on c5-t02 steering 30 (guard mustsay,leak) is a separate reply-layer fault. Found by Brain with check-run.mjs over director20's rows. Lesson: a predicate at zero means nothing until it has been run over rows known to hold the fault.
